name: GitHub
summary: Registering takes minutes and we found no approval step. The real decision is whether to use an OAuth app at all, because its scopes are broad and GitHub prefers GitHub Apps.
biggestRisk: An OAuth app's repo scope also grants access to code, which is a lot of power for an agent that only needs to read issues.

paths.name: Register an OAuth app
paths.whenToUse: You want your own name on the consent screen and broad scopes are acceptable.

wait.note: No approval step on this path.

steps.title: Choose the scopes your agent actually needs
steps.detail: List the agent's actions and map them to scopes. If the only fit is repo, read the note on GitHub Apps first.
steps.confirm: You have a short written list of scopes and a reason for each.

steps.title: Register the app
steps.detail: Go to Settings, Developer settings, OAuth apps, New OAuth App. Enter an application name, homepage URL and callback URL. Use the redirect URI from your Composio auth config as the callback.
steps.confirm: The app page shows a client ID.
steps.handoffReason: This requires signing in to your GitHub account.

steps.title: Generate a client secret
steps.detail: Generate a secret on the app page and paste it straight into Composio.
steps.confirm: Your Composio auth config saves and shows an ac_ ID.
steps.handoffReason: The secret should only be handled by you, not passed through an agent.

steps.title: Connect a test account
steps.detail: Complete one connection with your own account and check the consent screen shows your app's name.
steps.confirm: The agent can make one API call as that user.
steps.handoffReason: A person has to approve the consent screen.

blockers.symptom: The redirect fails with a redirect_uri mismatch
blockers.cause: With wildcard matching off, the redirect URL must exactly match the callback URL.
blockers.action: Copy the URI from Composio again. Check for trailing slashes and http versus https.

blockers.symptom: Older sessions start failing after repeated connections
blockers.cause: GitHub keeps ten tokens per user, app and scope combination, and revokes older ones beyond that.
blockers.action: Reuse stored connections so each reconnect doesn't mint a new token, especially in testing.

nuances.title: GitHub prefers GitHub Apps
nuances.detail: OAuth apps remain the right choice mainly when you need enterprise-level resources. Check that Composio's toolkit supports the flow you choose before you commit.

nuances.title: Broad scopes
nuances.detail: Reading issues or pull requests with an OAuth app takes the repo scope, which also covers code. That's a meaningful risk for an agent exposed to untrusted input.

nuances.title: Expiring tokens are on by default
nuances.detail: Your integration must handle refresh. Each refresh token is single-use, and the old pair stops working.

nuances.title: No automatic discovery
nuances.detail: GitHub didn't serve OIDC discovery at either standard path, so tools that auto-configure from metadata will need endpoints set by hand.
